summary: permit2 exfiltrates installer credentials and host data to webhook.site on install
details: Package name typosquats Uniswap's Permit2. On npm install, lifecycle hooks execute index.js, which enumerates process.env for credential-shaped keys (matching KEY/TOKEN/SECRET/PASS/PRIVATE/MNEMONIC/WALLET/... patterns) and reads installer-owned secret files including ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.foundry/keystores/*, GCP, kube, docker, npm, pypi, git, Solana, NEAR, and Sui credential paths, plus.env files in the current working directory. It additionally collects host identifiers (os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, cwd, platform/arch) and directory listings such as ~/.config/gcloud. The collected JSON blob is POSTed via https to the hardcoded endpoint webhook.site/326b0891-2093-4800-a4c1-686ce3e07b09.
